haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts it daily at 02:00 UTC. It extracts replica rows with updated_at later than the high-water mark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports keep transactions open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit. Visibility lags by up to 90 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: Its new updated_at makes a nightly extract re-read it within the lookback. Merge then overwrites the stored row since the staged updated_at is newer.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which also changes updated_at, so it arrives as an ordinary update. The row stays in fact_orders with is_deleted true.
haiku-low.q5: Failure is logged and rolled back. The scheduler retries after 15 minutes, up to three attempts total. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous complete night. A staleness alert goes to #data-alerts; running or waiting attempts continue.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation, once that week's nightly load commits. It compares order-creation days from the last 30 days by count and checksum, reloading mismatches.
haiku-low.q8: Merge keeps only the highest updated_at row per order_id. Upsert overwrites a stored row only if the staged updated_at is greater.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in warehouse table etl_watermark. Merge writes the highest updated_at extracted (unchanged if nothing extracted), in the same transaction as the load's commit.
haiku-low.q10: Merge commits the whole night in one warehouse transaction, so dashboards see all of it or none.
haiku-low.q11: The retry empties stg_orders first, discarding the failed attempt's staged rows. It extracts from the unchanged high-water mark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads all of that day's rows from the replica into stg_recon, then merges them into fact_orders in one newer-wins transaction. The mark stays put.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts it at 02:00 UTC daily (logging a running etl_runs row). It extracts orders from the app's Postgres read replica whose updated_at is later than the high-water mark minus 2 hours (everything on the first run).
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports can keep a transaction open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time. So a row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
sonnet.q3: The edit changes updated_at, so the next nightly extract (updated_at > mark - 2h) pulls it into staging, and merge upserts it into fact_orders because its updated_at is greater than the stored one.
sonnet.q4: The app soft-deletes (sets deleted_at, which also changes updated_at). It reaches the warehouse as an ordinary update; fact_orders keeps the row with is_deleted = true.
sonnet.q5: The failure is logged (job marks its etl_runs row failed with error text, or the scheduler does for crash, kill, hang or never-start). Transaction rolls back; mark and fact_orders unchanged. The scheduler waits 15 minutes and restarts the whole job as a new attempt (up to 3 attempts total). After the third failure it pages on-call.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous complete night. The 06:00 UTC check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts (if no nightly attempt for that night has succeeded).
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation: it compares per-day row counts and checksums (order_id + updated_at) for the last 30 days, reloads mismatched days from the replica into stg_recon and merges them into fact_orders. (It only runs if that Sunday's nightly load succeeded.)
sonnet.q8: Merge keeps only the highest-updated_at row per order_id in staging, and the upsert into fact_orders overwrites only if the staged updated_at is greater than the stored one, so older or identical rows change nothing.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark. It is set to the highest updated_at extracted (unchanged if nothing was extracted), written inside the Merge transaction, at the same commit that upserts fact_orders and marks the run success. It never moves back.
sonnet.q10: Merge into fact_orders and the mark advance happen in one warehouse transaction that commits atomically, so dashboards (refreshing from fact_orders at 06:00) see either the whole night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: stg_orders is emptied at the start of the retry's Extract, so leftovers are discarded. The retry reruns the whole job from Extract using the unchanged mark, so it extracts rows with updated_at later than the old mark minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads all of that mismatched day's rows from the replica into stg_recon, then merges them into fact_orders with the same merge logic as step 3 (only overwrite if newer) in one transaction. It does not change the high-water mark.
